title: SE Rapid Proof: Compact Experiment Deck (WIP)
content:
Deck goal:
- Give SEs a short, reproducible slide deck and runbook to execute a 2-week 'rapid proof' pilot that demonstrates latency, cost, and reliability tradeoffs for a small integration (chat + embeddings).

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (integration lead)
- Product manager (pilot owner)
- SE / Solutions engineer (you)

One-line value prop to lead with:
- Show measurable latency and token-cost improvements (or graceful fallbacks) in 10–14 calendar days using Redwood’s hosted + dedicated routing pattern.

Deck flow (10 slides / 8–12 minute demo):
1) Title + TL;DR (30s)
   - Speaker note: set expectations — outcome is a short report with numbers and a recommended config for onramp.
2) Problem framing (45s)
   - High-level: unpredictable inference cost, latency spikes, hard to reason about fallbacks when capacity drops.
   - Quick stat to prompt interest: "Median tail P95 latency difference across embedded infra: X ms" (replace with pilot numbers).
3) What Redwood does for this pilot (60s)
   - Routing: hosted \u2192 dedicated fallbacks
   - Cost levers: batching, prefix caching, quantization suggestions
   - Observability: per-route token/latency breakdowns in Console.
4) Pilot scope & success metrics (60s)
   - Workload: 1k daily users, two routes: chat (L) and semantic-search (S)
   - Baselines: current provider or internal endpoint metrics for latency, cost per 1k queries, error rate
   - Success criteria (one or more): P95 latency reduction >= 20% OR cost per inference <= baseline by >= 15% without >2x error rate.
5) Technical architecture (90s)
   - Diagram (slide): client -> Redwood Edge -> routing policy -> model variants (fast/cheap/robust) -> KV-cache layer
   - Speaker note: emphasize easy pinning of model versions and automatic compatible fallbacks.
6) Runbook (2 slides)
   - Step 0: pre-checks (API key, model catalog access, sample corpus)
   - Step 1: enable hosted route, collect 48h baseline
   - Step 2: configure dedicated routing with burst policy, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts
   - Step 3: enable lightweight batching (samples in Console) and run A/B for 3 days each
   - Step 4: export token/latency traces and run provided eval script (link in runbook)
7) Short demo script (live or recorded) (2–3 minutes)
   - 3 quick actions: show Console route creation, toggle fallback variant, show a trace for a slow request and how it reroutes
8) Competitive checks & selling points for this pilot (90s)
   - If asked about vendor X: emphasize unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, predictable reserved capacity, and built-in fallbacks for reliability
   - If asked about going self-hosted: highlight time-to-result (2 weeks vs months) and integrated observability tied to cost metrics
9) Risks & mitigations (60s)
   - Risk: dataset/profile mismatches -> Mitigation: sample generator and warm-up run included
   - Risk: enterprise security concerns -> Mitigation: run pilot in Private mode for sensitive data; KMS/HSM options available
10) Close: asks and next steps (30s)
   - Ask the customer to approve 2-week pilot window, share a representative corpus (<= 10k queries), and nominate a technical contact

Appendix (runbook details and templates)
- Pre-check checklist (copyable): API key present, allowed inbound IPs, sample prompt set, expected QPS, SLO targets
- Quick config snippets (curl + SDK) for: creating route, enabling dedicated fallback, setting batching policy
- Eval script outline: run 500 synthetic prompts, measure token counts, P50/P95/P99 latencies, error types, and cost per token.

Sample objection handling (short bullets):
- "We need to own the model" -> "You can pin model versions in Redwood, or use Private to host the runtime; pilot proves the routing and cost controls first."
- "What if dedicated capacity isn't worth it for us?" -> "Pilot includes a mixed routing run to show marginal benefit; we can recommend keep vs buy after data."
- "How do fallbacks affect output quality?" -> "We include quality monitors and prompt-based evals. If fallback affects accuracy, we can adjust policies or use constrained fallbacks for critical routes."

Measurement plan (for SE to commit to delivering results)
- Day 0–2: baseline collection on current infra (or Redwood hosted)
- Day 3–9: A/B with batching and cache enabled on half traffic
- Day 10–12: dedicated routing enabled + canary to 10% then 100%
- Deliverable: 2-page pilot report with numbers, 3 recommended configs, and a follow-up one-hour review session

Logistics checklist for SEs (copyable):
- Book a 30-minute kickoff with customer and the internal SRE contact
- Create pilot Confluence page (template link in linked_artifacts)
- Assign postmortem owner and date

Speaker quick scripts (30s stubs to hand to junior SEs):
- Kickoff: "Goal for this run is to produce a single, actionable recommendation on routing and caching that reduces P95 latency or cost per call. We'll run minimal changes and measure after 10 days."
- Demo transition: "I'll flip the routing policy now; you should see the Console trace show a different model variant and an immediate latency delta."

Notes to self (SE edits / open questions):
- Need to add a slide with example numbers from last pilot (Marco to add)
- Validate the eval script works with both chat and embedding endpoints (Ethan owns)

Bottom line: this is a compact, reproducible pilot deck that helps SEs get quantitative results quickly and gives customers a low-friction path to test Redwood’s routing and cost controls.
